Attributes and its types  • An entity is represented by a set of attributes, that is  descriptive properties possessed by all members of an entity  set.
subject: dbms

text: A. Simple Attribute  Simple attributes are those that are atomic (Not  Divisible).  Example: Roll_no, Class and Age.    B. Composite Attributes  Composite attributes are those that can be further subdivided into simpler  parts. Here, the attributes “Name” and “Address” are composite attributes  as they are composed of many other simple attributes.    C. Single Valued Attribute  Single valued attributes are those attributes which can take only one value  for a given entity from an entity set.  Here, all the attributes are single valued attributes as they can take only  one specific value for each entity.
subject: dbms

text: D. Multi-Valued Attributes  Multi valued attributes are those attributes which can take more than one  value for a given entity from an entity set.  Here, the attributes “Mob_no” and “Email_id” are multi valued attributes  as they can take more than one values for a given entity.      E. Derived Attributes  Derived attributes are those attributes which can be derived from other  attribute(s).  Here, the attribute “Age” is a derived attribute as it can be derived from the  attribute “DOB”.
subject: dbms

text: F. Key Attributes  Key attributes are those attributes which can identify an entity uniquely in  an entity set.  Here, the attribute “Roll_no” is a key attribute as it can identify any  student uniquely.    2. Logical vs Physical data Independence    3. Three schema Architecture  Proposed to support DBMS characteristics of:  a. Program-data independence.  b. Support of multiple views of the data.  Not explicitly used in commercial DBMS products, but has been useful in  explaining database system organization

text: • Defines DBMS schemas at three levels:  a. Internal schema at the internal level to describe physical storage  structures and access paths (e.g indexes).  • Typically uses a physical data model.  b. Conceptual schema at the conceptual level to describe the  structure and constraints for the whole database for a  community of users.  • Uses a conceptual or an implementation data model.  c. External schemas at the external level to describe the various  user views.  • Usually uses the same data model as the conceptual  schema.    4. Advantages Of DBMS Approach  1.  •  Data Redundancy Control  DBMS reduces duplication of data by storing it in a centralized  database.  2.  •  Data Consistency  Since redundancy is controlled, the same data remains consistent  across the system.
subject: dbms

text: 3.  •  Data Sharing  Multiple users and applications can access and share the same  database simultaneously.  4.  •  Data Security  DBMS provides authorization and access control to protect sensitive  data.  5.  •  Data Integrity  It ensures accuracy and reliability of data through constraints and  rules.  6.  •  Backup and Recovery  DBMS provides mechanisms to recover data in case of system failure  or data loss.  5. These are usually specified in an ad-hoc  manner through DBMS design and administration manuals  • Implementation (representational) data models:  • Provide concepts that fall between the above two, used by  many commercial DBMS implementations (e.g. relational  data models used in many commercial systems).  • Self-Describing Data Models:  • Combine the description of data with the data values.  Examples include XML, key-value stores and some NOSQL  systems.
